doc.title: Luis Conte interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 24, 2025

title: Bringing the right gear: Don Alias and Madonna stories, cartage
summary: Conte discusses what percussion producers ask for, compares Don Alias's Jagger session with his own Dick Tracy session playing only triangle, and explains carrying many instruments via Angel City Drum Works.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Do they give you a heads up about the session and say please bring X, please bring this and that.

On film work a lot of the times, yeah. Film work yeah. But on records yes, sometimes there is sometimes they may say, “Hey by the way do you have udus?” You know it’s this clay pot, you know it’s something special they would ask. Yeah, yeah. Okay, I think we’re going to need some of those you know. But I have a really good assortment of stuff that I send. So a lot of times I’m not really missing much of what they need. You know but at times they do ask for certain things, they may ask for a frame drum. You know, or an Irish drum, a bodhran or something like that. I’ve got it. “I’m glad you told me because I wouldn’t have sent it.”
I have a little story here from Don Alias.

I was able to speak with him and he had this story that he got a call to play with a Mick Jagger recording and he said, “I brought every piece of percussion I could get my hands on: littlest shakers, big drums, small drums, tambourines, a whole van load. I wanted to be ready. Turns out all they wanted me to do was play fills on a syn drum. You know? Boom. So I sat there for six hours going boom.”

Yup. Well I wanted to do a Madonna recording and I sent everything I thought, because it was for the movie Dick Tracy. I sent everything I own. And I ended up playing triangle. It was triangle on this one song [scats]. “Okay great, we got it, thanks Luis,” “Okay, see ya.” So you never know.
Do you get paid by the note?

Yeah. But you know you have to have – the other thing I learned early on is it’s not just one cowbell, it’s a whole bunch of cowbells. It’s not just one triangle, it’s a bunch of triangles. It’s not just one shaker, it’s a bunch of shakers. Because there’s a track – this particular cowbell may not really work with a triangle, do you have a different tone. You know. You learn, there’s a lot – you need a lot of stuff. Because you don’t know.
That’s a good quote. You need a lot of stuff.
Yeah man, we need a lot of stuff. I got a lot of stuff. I got so much gear I don't know what to do with it.
Do you have a cartage system? You know have people move stuff around for you?

Yeah. Angel City Drum Works is the name of the company and they have like – I think I’m the only percussion player they have, but they have a lot of drummers. Erskine, Peter Erskine, JR, a bunch of cats. And they take us around in the studios. But the new world now is having a home recording studio you know. So I have one and thank God I’ve been pretty busy about it, with it. And a lot of sessions happen now that you don’t go anywhere, you just do them here. Overdubs.
